jobs.title: Director - Finance, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
About The Foundation

At the St. Joseph’s Health Centre Foundation we are committed to continuing to transform St. Joe’s as a leading community hospital that delivers the best care experiences to Toronto’s west end. We are guided by our mission to inspire philanthropy from our community and raise the funds needed to support that transformation.

St. Joe’s has provided care for millions of people in Toronto’s west end for more than a century. Today it is one Canada’s busiest community teaching hospitals, looking after a vibrant community of over half a million.

The Foundation has grown in recent years to be a leading community hospital foundation with a strong and engaged board of directors. We are looking for a new team member to help with gift management and donor engagement that helps to deliver the best care possible for our community.

About The Position

The Director, Finance, Data & Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership across financial management, business intelligence, fundraising analytics and organizational performance for the Foundation.

As the Foundation enters an ambitious next phase of campaign growth, this role will be responsible for ensuring that the organization has the financial discipline, data infrastructure and insights required to support informed decision-making and maximize fundraising performance.

Working closely with the President & CEO, VP, Operations, Senior Leadership Team and fundraising leaders, the Director will connect financial and fundraising data to provide a clear, timely and actionable view of organizational and campaign performance.

The Director will be the Foundation’s lead resource for financial reporting, fundraising analytics, campaign intelligence, data quality and performance reporting, ensuring that leaders have the information they need to identify opportunities, manage risk, allocate resources and achieve campaign objectives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise with an analytical and business-oriented mindset, an understanding of fundraising and donor data, and the ability to translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Management
Lead the Foundation’s financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting processes.
Prepare timely, accurate decision-useful financial reports for the President & CEO, Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee and Board.
Monitor financial performance against budget and provide analysis of material variances, trends, risks and opportunities.
Lead the annual budgeting and collaborate on the business planning process with the VP, Operations and Senior Leadership Team.
Oversee cash flow, investments, receivables, payables and other core financial management activities.
Lead the annual audit and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures.
Ensure appropriate financial oversight of designated funds, restricted gifts, commitments and disbursements.
Work closely with external accounting and investment partners as required.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements and Foundation policies.
Campaign & Fundraising Analytics
Own the development and ongoing management of the Foundation’s campaign reporting and fundraising analytics framework.
Partner with fundraising leadership to establish clear definitions, methodologies and performance measures for campaign pipeline, proposals, asks, commitments and revenue.
Develop and maintain campaign dashboards that provide management and Board-level visibility into campaign progress and future potential.
Provide analysis that identifies emerging gaps, opportunities and trends and supports proactive campaign management.
Develop forecasting models to support campaign revenue projections and scenario planning.
Work with fundraising leaders to assess portfolio capacity, prospect movement and pipeline sufficiency.
Translate fundraising data into concise insights and recommendations for the Senior Leadership Team, Campaign Leadership, Finance Committee and Board.
Data Strategy, Quality & Business Intelligence
Serve as the Foundation’s internal lead for data strategy, data governance and business intelligence.
Establish standards for data quality, consistency, definitions and reporting across financial and fundraising systems and oversee implantation with Database Manager.
Partner with fundraising and operations teams to improve the use of Raiser's Edge NXT and other systems as strategic management tools.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting and improve data accessibility.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools using appropriate business intelligence platforms.
Connect financial, fundraising, donor and operational data to provide a more complete picture of organizational performance.
Establish appropriate data governance, privacy, security and access practices in partnership with organizational leadership.
Identify technology and systems improvements that will increase efficiency, insight and fundraising productivity.
Prospect & Donor Intelligence
Support the fundraising team with data-driven prospect identification, qualification and prioritization.
Develop reporting to help assess prospect capacity, relationship activity, portfolio composition and movement through the fundraising cycle.
Partner with fundraising leadership to identify gaps in prospect pipelines and opportunities for portfolio development.
Support analysis of donor behaviour, giving patterns, retention, upgrades and other trends that inform fundraising strategy.
Organizational Performance & Decision Support
Working with VP, Operations develop a consistent framework of organizational KPIs aligned with the Foundation’s strategic and business plans.
Provide analysis to support resource allocation, staffing decisions, event and program performance, fundraising investments and operational planning.
Identify trends and insights across revenue, expenses, fundraising activity and organizational performance.
Prepare clear, concise analysis and visualizations for leadership and Board audiences.
Act as a strategic thought partner to leaders, moving beyond reporting results to helping the organization understand what the data means and what action it should inform.
Leadership, Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Lead continuous improvement of financial and fundraising reporting processes.
Provide leadership and coaching to the administration team, including the Database Manager.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, automate repetitive activities and improve organizational efficiency.
Contribute to a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide leadership and coaching to staff, contractors or external resources supporting finance, data and analytics.

Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, financial management, analytics, business intelligence or a related field.
Experience working in a nonprofit, healthcare, fundraising or similarly complex environment is an asset.
Demonstrated experience developing budgets, forecasts, financial models and management reporting.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into clear business insights.
Experience with CRM and fundraising databases; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT is an asset.
Experience developing dashboards and reporting using tools such as Power BI or equivalent is an asset.
Experience working with large or complex datasets and improving data quality and reporting processes.
Strong understanding of data governance, privacy and information management.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to present financial and analytical information clearly.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strategic, curious and improvement-oriented.

jobs.title: Director, Digital Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Our mission is to Drive Business Performance. We use data to create personalized and connected experiences that deliver transformative business outcomes. Our role is to ensure our clients meet their quantifiable business goals every day, consistently, in every market. We are entirely focused on delivering better business results through optimization, creation and analysis across all digital platforms. Our scope ranges from recommending how to use content more effectively to optimizing daily media channel performance and maximizing visibility in eCommerce platforms.

The Director, Digital Strategy is the senior strategic digital lead for the client account. The role defines how digital channels work together across the customer journey to support the client’s brand and business goals, and ensures digital thinking is embedded from the brief onward rather than added once activation begins.This is a client-facing leadership role focused on vision, integration and decision-making. The Director turns audience, cultural, platform, business and measurement signals into a focused digital strategy, clear priorities and practical roadmaps. The role brings choiceful recommendations, constructive challenge and a future-facing point of view.

The Director will work alongside Client Leadership and Planning, while partnering closely with the Digital Manager, channel specialists and Media Effectiveness. The Digital Manager and specialists remain responsible for in-platform strategy, buying, account structure, bidding, pacing, optimization, trafficking and quality assurance. The Director sets the strategic direction and ensures the work adds up to one connected digital proposition.

What Success Looks Like

The client can clearly articulate the digital channel strategy, the role of each channel and how the ecosystem supports business growth.
Digital strategy develops at the same pace as the broader media strategy and shapes investment, audience and measurement decisions from the outset.
The client receives concise, decisive recommendations that clarify what matters now, what comes next and why.
Testing, measurement and learning lead to visible changes in strategy, investment and activation.
First-party data, audience and innovation opportunities progress through practical, phased roadmaps with clear ownership and dependencies.
The account operates as one integrated client leadership, planning, digital activation and measurement team.

Key Accountabilities

Digital channel strategy and integration

Own the account’s digital channel strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, audience needs, customer journey, channel roles, investment priorities and measurement
Partner with Client Leadership and Planning from the brief onward so digital strategy is developed as part of the core media response, not as a downstream activation layer.
Define how paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display, Video and other relevant digital channels work together across the funnel, while channel specialists determine the detailed in-platform approach.
Translate complex inputs into a focused set of priorities, choices and actions the client and team can understand and deliver.

Audience, innovation and growth agenda

Develop audience and segmentation strategies that connect broad media audiences, platform signals, app and loyalty opportunities, and first-party data ambitions.
Identify opportunities to improve brand impact, acquisition, engagement, loyalty and media effectiveness, and convert them into sequenced recommendations with clear expected value.
Bring a forward-looking point of view on changing consumer behaviour, platform evolution, AI-enabled media and emerging digital opportunities, distinguishing useful innovation from novelty.
Create a visible innovation agenda for the client that links new opportunities to real business questions, readiness and measurable outcomes.

Measurement, testing and learnin g

With Media Effectiveness and channel leads, define the learning agenda and ensure each priority has a clear business question, hypothesis, success measure and decision rule.
Connect reach, attention, engagement, conversion, efficiency and incrementality evidence to the business question being answered.
Turn reporting and specialist input into concise recommendations on what to continue, change, stop, scale or test next.
Ensure learning is applied back into audience, channel, investment and creative decisions, creating a continuous strategy-to-learning cycle.

First-party data and connected capabilities

Lead the media strategy and use-case components of the first-party data and audience maturity roadmap, in partnership with Media Effectiveness, CRM, loyalty, app, privacy, data and technology stakeholders.
Break complex ambitions into practical phases with explicit ownership, dependencies, decision points and realistic timelines.
First party data connecting to business strategy

Client leadership and team developmen t

Present the digital strategy and roadmap in senior meetings, annual planning, business reviews and critical transformation workstreams.
Coach the Digital Manager, planners and specialists to connect platform recommendations to the wider strategy and communicate with greater clarity and confidence.
Establish clear ways of working and decision rights across Client Leadership, Planning, Digital Activation, Media Effectiveness and specialist partners.

Qualifications

8+ years of progressive experience in digital media strategy, communications planning, digital transformation or integrated media, ideally across agency and/or client environments.
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Media, Advertising, Marketing, Business, Strategy, Analytics or a related field
Demonstrated experience building full-funnel digital channel strategies that connect business goals, audiences, channel roles, investment and measurement.
Strong understanding of the strategic roles and interdependencies of paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display and Video. Current platform fluency is required; deep hands-on buying or platform-operations expertise is not the core requirement.
Experience translating audience, platform, analytics, research and business signals into a clear strategic point of view and actionable roadmap.
Practical understanding of first-party data, CRM, app and loyalty use cases, including the organizational and measurement dependencies required to activate them.
Experience shaping learning agendas and working with measurement specialists to turn evidence into decisions.
Exceptional client leadership, storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to simplify complexity and make decisive recommendations.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing outcomes without relying solely on formal authority.

Additional Information

jobs.title: Principal Creative Director, AI Video
jobs.description:
Who We Are Is What We Do.

Deel is the all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. Our vision is to unlock global opportunity for every person, team, and business. Built for the way the world works today, Deel combines HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits, performance, and equipment management into one seamless platform. With AI-powered tools and a fully owned payroll infrastructure, Deel supports every worker type in 150+ countries—helping businesses scale smarter, faster, and more compliantly.

Among the largest globally distributed companies in the world, our team of 7,000 spans more than 100 countries, speaks 74 languages, and brings a connected and dynamic culture that drives continuous learning and innovation for our customers.

Why should you be part of our success story?

As the fastest-growing Software as a Service (SaaS) company in history, Deel is transforming how global talent connects with world-class companies – breaking down borders that have traditionally limited both hiring and career opportunities. We're not just building software; we're creating the infrastructure for the future of work, enabling a more diverse and inclusive global economy. In 2024 alone, we paid $11.2 billion to workers in nearly 100 currencies and provided healthcare and benefits to workers in 109 countries—ensuring people get paid and protected, no matter where they are.

Our momentum is reflected in our achievements and customer satisfaction: CNBC Disruptor 50, Forbes Cloud 100, Deloitte Fast 500, and repeated recognition on Y Combinator's top companies list – all while maintaining a 4.83 average rating from 15,000 reviews across G2, Trustpilot, Captera, Apple and Google.

Your experience at Deel will be a career accelerator. At the forefront of the global work revolution, you'll tackle complex challenges that impact millions of people's working lives. With our momentum—backed by a $17.3 billion valuation and $1 B in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) in just over five years—you'll drive meaningful impact while building expertise that makes you a sought-after leader in the transformation of global work.

About The Studio

Deel is one of the fastest-growing companies in the world, and we're building the brand and creative studio to match. We make global campaigns, partnerships, film, design, and social at real scale, for businesses and for workers in almost every country there is.

We're looking for someone exceptional to raise the bar on what we make. This is a hands-on role. You'd set the standard by making the work.

The role

Deel is a truly global, people-first brand, and it's taking off. We're looking for a creative director who works at the front edge of AI-native production across video and design. Most AI creative work is technically impressive and creatively empty. Some of it is good work that used AI somewhere in the pipeline. We think there's a real discipline in between, and we want you to build it here. You'd define how we make this work, and you'd prove it by making it. This is a hands-on role.

What You'll Make

AI-native creative. Work where generative tools are central to how it's made, at a standard the category hasn't reached.
The stack. Our AI creative tooling and the workflows around it, including the principles for where we don't use it.
Video and motion. Brand films, campaign work, and product storytelling that blend traditional and AI-led production.
A repeatable method. Something the rest of the team can use, so the capability outlives any one project.

What You Bring

At least ten years across video, motion, or design, with direction as well as production.
Recent work made or directed with generative AI that stands up as creative work first.
Deep knowledge of the current tooling, and clear judgment about where it breaks.
Proven ability to build a workflow other people can actually use.
A point of view on likeness, disclosure, and provenance. We take these seriously.

What Would Set You Apart

A reel with range across live-action, motion, and generative work.
Experience establishing an AI practice inside a creative team.
A public point of view on AI in creative work.

Who You'll Work With

You'll sit inside the creative studio and work alongside our Creative Director, the video and motion teams, and the brand designers who'll build on what you establish.

How We Work

We're a studio, not a request queue. People here make things rather than manage from a distance. We use AI seriously, and we're deliberate about where we don't.

Recruiting timelines vary by position, however, all Deel positions accept applications for a minimum of 5 days from the posting date listed herein. This position is open and still accepting applications

Total Rewards

Our workforce deserves fair and competitive pay that meets them where they are. With scalable benefits, rewards, and perks, our total rewards programs reflect our commitment to inclusivity and access for all.

Our salary range reflects gross base salary. For commercial roles with commission eligibility, this figure represents On-Target Earnings (OTE), inclusive of base salary and target commission.
Salary ranges are quoted in USD as a consistent global reference. Your offer will be localized to your country's currency using a market-aligned conversion.
Final pay is based on objective, job-related criteria including experience, skills, and location.
We don't ask about salary history. Offers are based on the role and what you bring to it.

Some things you'll enjoy

Stock grant opportunities dependent on your role, employment status and location
Additional perks and benefits based on your employment status and country
Optional flexible working office membership, with IWG

At Deel, we're an equal-opportunity employer that values diversity and positively encourage applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of race, religion, sex, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy or maternity or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Unless otherwise agreed, we will communicate with job applicants using Deel-specific emails, which include @ deel.com and other acquired company emails like @ payspace.com and @ paygroup.com . You can view the most up-to-date job listings at Deel by visiting our careers page .

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.title: Associate Director, Commercial Banking (Corporate Finance Group)
jobs.description:
Corporate Finance Team Overview:

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview

The Associate Director plays a critical role in supporting the growth and risk‑management objectives of the portfolio. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.
Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions
Monitors the portfolio performance for assigned portfolio of Commercial Banking clients on an ongoing basis, taking corrective action when required.
Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded. Escalates issues when needed.
Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Preferred 5 – 7 years of relevant experience in credit or lending instruments or financial operations in a corporate or banking environment.
If a Credit Qualifiable job, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
Deep knowledge and technical proficiency gained through extensive education and business experience.

Foundational level of proficiency:

Structuring Deals

Advanced level of proficiency:

Problem Solving
Collaboration
Detail-Oriented
Customer Service
Loan Structuring
Regulatory Compliance
Portfolio Management
Credit Risk Assessment
Banking Operations
Microsoft Office

Expert level of proficiency:

Financial analysis

Salary:

$70,000.00 - $150,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

jobs.title: Director, Private Capital, Financial Services
jobs.description:
The opportunity

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board (Ontario Teachers') is a global investor with net assets of ~$279 billion as of December 31, 2025. Ontario Teachers’ is a fully funded defined benefit pension plan, and it invests in a broad array of asset classes to deliver retirement security for 346,000 working members and pensioners. Our Private Capital group deploys ~$60 billion across direct private equity investments and private equity funds globally.

The Director will be a senior member of our Financial Services investment team — partnering with our Senior Managing Directors and Managing Directors to source, diligence, execute, and direct private equity investments in the Financial Services sector. This is a development seat with a clear path toward independent deal leadership for a candidate who has already built a strong foundation in private equity investing.

Who You'll Work With

Reporting to the Managing Director, the role will be part of a deal team comprising analysts, associates, principals, directors, and managing directors, supported by third-party consultants, operating executives, and legal and accounting advisors dedicated to each transaction.

The Financial Services team invests across sub-sectors including Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments, with particular need to understand the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping the sector. The role will also potentially partner with colleagues in OTPP's global offices on international investment and / or cross asset class opportunities in Financial Services.

What You'll Do

Serve as a key member of deal teams — conducting industry and company due diligence, building financial models, arranging debt financing, negotiating legal documents, and preparing written recommendations for the Underwriting Committee.
Lead or co-lead individual deals and workstreams with oversight from the SMD or MD; own specific diligence streams (financial, operational, commercial, legal, tax, insurance) end-to-end.
Post-close, remain actively involved with portfolio companies — often as board observer or board member — working with management on strategy, value creation, M&A, and refinancing.
Contribute to deal flow generation through desk research, consultant relationships, operating executive networks, conferences, and relationships with management teams.
Lead sub-sector deep dives and thematic research as the team evolves its coverage strategy, including emerging AI, regulatory, and digitization themes.
Manage and develop analysts, associates, and principals on deal teams; provide direct mentorship on diligence, modeling, judgment, and communication.
Work in a highly collaborative manner, bringing a complex network of stakeholders along (Global and Sector SMDs, MDs, deal teams, Portfolio Solutions team, international office leaders, portfolio companies, etc.). Strike the appropriate balance of being a confident decision-maker and an inclusive leader.
Build a network of operating executives, CEOs, consultants, bankers, and peer sponsors; progress toward independent deal sourcing by the end of Director tenure.
Develop value creation expertise in close partnership with the SMD and MDs; contribute to portfolio company initiatives as assigned.
Exercise judgment within deal teams and surface recommendations to the MD or SMD; lead individual workstreams and, over time, full deals with oversight.
Provide disciplined thinking, sound judgment, and courage of conviction, with a willingness to take balanced, thesis-driven risk. Intervene directly and effectively when required and escalate issues early.
Work cross-functionally and collaboratively with other teams to ensure continued alignment with OTPP's mission, vision, and values — including supporting and sharing knowledge with other areas of Investments and responding to ad hoc requests.

What You'll Need

~10+ years of meaningful work experience, including several years of recent private equity investing. Active M&A in a senior role in corporate development would also be considered. Supplemented by previous experience in management consulting, investment banking, and/or corporations (preferably corporate development or similar roles).
Experience playing a lead role on deal workstreams, including conducting due diligence, leading multiple diligence streams (financial, operational, legal, tax, insurance), arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Direct investment exposure to Financial Services preferred.
Familiarity with Financial Services sector dynamics — particularly Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments — and the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping them
Some experience serving on “for profit” Boards of Directors or board committees a plus.
Strong academic background, with a financial designation (MBA, CFA, CBV, or CA strongly preferred).
Experience playing a leading role in the investment process, including conducting due diligence, arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Strong negotiating skills.
Ability to balance priorities, work independently, lead projects, and thrive in a high-performance team environment.
Very strong analytical and quantitative skills to perform and guide in-depth, innovative, critical analysis.
Deep understanding of fundamental investment analysis and private equity value creation.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build constructive relationships with internal and external parties, particularly management teams, boards, and senior advisors.
Strong communication skills, both oral and written, including IC paper authorship and presentation.
Willingness and ability to travel across North America and globally.

What We’re Offering

Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development
Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage
Retirement income through a defined benefit pension plan
The opportunity to invest back into the fund through our Deferred Incentive Program
A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working
Competitive time off

new_jobs.title: Director, Digital Strategy
new_jobs.description:
Job Description:

Our mission is to Drive Business Performance. We use data to create personalized and connected experiences that deliver transformative business outcomes. Our role is to ensure our clients meet their quantifiable business goals every day, consistently, in every market. We are entirely focused on delivering better business results through optimization, creation and analysis across all digital platforms. Our scope ranges from recommending how to use content more effectively to optimizing daily media channel performance and maximizing visibility in eCommerce platforms.

The Director, Digital Strategy is the senior strategic digital lead for the client account. The role defines how digital channels work together across the customer journey to support the client’s brand and business goals, and ensures digital thinking is embedded from the brief onward rather than added once activation begins.This is a client-facing leadership role focused on vision, integration and decision-making. The Director turns audience, cultural, platform, business and measurement signals into a focused digital strategy, clear priorities and practical roadmaps. The role brings choiceful recommendations, constructive challenge and a future-facing point of view.

The Director will work alongside Client Leadership and Planning, while partnering closely with the Digital Manager, channel specialists and Media Effectiveness. The Digital Manager and specialists remain responsible for in-platform strategy, buying, account structure, bidding, pacing, optimization, trafficking and quality assurance. The Director sets the strategic direction and ensures the work adds up to one connected digital proposition.

What Success Looks Like

The client can clearly articulate the digital channel strategy, the role of each channel and how the ecosystem supports business growth.
Digital strategy develops at the same pace as the broader media strategy and shapes investment, audience and measurement decisions from the outset.
The client receives concise, decisive recommendations that clarify what matters now, what comes next and why.
Testing, measurement and learning lead to visible changes in strategy, investment and activation.
First-party data, audience and innovation opportunities progress through practical, phased roadmaps with clear ownership and dependencies.
The account operates as one integrated client leadership, planning, digital activation and measurement team.

Key Accountabilities

Digital channel strategy and integration

Own the account’s digital channel strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, audience needs, customer journey, channel roles, investment priorities and measurement
Partner with Client Leadership and Planning from the brief onward so digital strategy is developed as part of the core media response, not as a downstream activation layer.
Define how paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display, Video and other relevant digital channels work together across the funnel, while channel specialists determine the detailed in-platform approach.
Translate complex inputs into a focused set of priorities, choices and actions the client and team can understand and deliver.

Audience, innovation and growth agenda

Develop audience and segmentation strategies that connect broad media audiences, platform signals, app and loyalty opportunities, and first-party data ambitions.
Identify opportunities to improve brand impact, acquisition, engagement, loyalty and media effectiveness, and convert them into sequenced recommendations with clear expected value.
Bring a forward-looking point of view on changing consumer behaviour, platform evolution, AI-enabled media and emerging digital opportunities, distinguishing useful innovation from novelty.
Create a visible innovation agenda for the client that links new opportunities to real business questions, readiness and measurable outcomes.

Measurement, testing and learnin g

With Media Effectiveness and channel leads, define the learning agenda and ensure each priority has a clear business question, hypothesis, success measure and decision rule.
Connect reach, attention, engagement, conversion, efficiency and incrementality evidence to the business question being answered.
Turn reporting and specialist input into concise recommendations on what to continue, change, stop, scale or test next.
Ensure learning is applied back into audience, channel, investment and creative decisions, creating a continuous strategy-to-learning cycle.

First-party data and connected capabilities

Lead the media strategy and use-case components of the first-party data and audience maturity roadmap, in partnership with Media Effectiveness, CRM, loyalty, app, privacy, data and technology stakeholders.
Break complex ambitions into practical phases with explicit ownership, dependencies, decision points and realistic timelines.
First party data connecting to business strategy

Client leadership and team developmen t

Present the digital strategy and roadmap in senior meetings, annual planning, business reviews and critical transformation workstreams.
Coach the Digital Manager, planners and specialists to connect platform recommendations to the wider strategy and communicate with greater clarity and confidence.
Establish clear ways of working and decision rights across Client Leadership, Planning, Digital Activation, Media Effectiveness and specialist partners.

Qualifications

8+ years of progressive experience in digital media strategy, communications planning, digital transformation or integrated media, ideally across agency and/or client environments.
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Media, Advertising, Marketing, Business, Strategy, Analytics or a related field
Demonstrated experience building full-funnel digital channel strategies that connect business goals, audiences, channel roles, investment and measurement.
Strong understanding of the strategic roles and interdependencies of paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display and Video. Current platform fluency is required; deep hands-on buying or platform-operations expertise is not the core requirement.
Experience translating audience, platform, analytics, research and business signals into a clear strategic point of view and actionable roadmap.
Practical understanding of first-party data, CRM, app and loyalty use cases, including the organizational and measurement dependencies required to activate them.
Experience shaping learning agendas and working with measurement specialists to turn evidence into decisions.
Exceptional client leadership, storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to simplify complexity and make decisive recommendations.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing outcomes without relying solely on formal authority.

Who We Are Is What We Do.

Deel is the all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. Our vision is to unlock global opportunity for every person, team, and business. Built for the way the world works today, Deel combines HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits, performance, and equipment management into one seamless platform. With AI-powered tools and a fully owned payroll infrastructure, Deel supports every worker type in 150+ countries—helping businesses scale smarter, faster, and more compliantly.

Among the largest globally distributed companies in the world, our team of 7,000 spans more than 100 countries, speaks 74 languages, and brings a connected and dynamic culture that drives continuous learning and innovation for our customers.

Why should you be part of our success story?

As the fastest-growing Software as a Service (SaaS) company in history, Deel is transforming how global talent connects with world-class companies – breaking down borders that have traditionally limited both hiring and career opportunities. We're not just building software; we're creating the infrastructure for the future of work, enabling a more diverse and inclusive global economy. In 2024 alone, we paid $11.2 billion to workers in nearly 100 currencies and provided healthcare and benefits to workers in 109 countries—ensuring people get paid and protected, no matter where they are.

Our momentum is reflected in our achievements and customer satisfaction: CNBC Disruptor 50, Forbes Cloud 100, Deloitte Fast 500, and repeated recognition on Y Combinator's top companies list – all while maintaining a 4.83 average rating from 15,000 reviews across G2, Trustpilot, Captera, Apple and Google.

Your experience at Deel will be a career accelerator. At the forefront of the global work revolution, you'll tackle complex challenges that impact millions of people's working lives. With our momentum—backed by a $17.3 billion valuation and $1 B in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) in just over five years—you'll drive meaningful impact while building expertise that makes you a sought-after leader in the transformation of global work.

About The Studio

Deel is one of the fastest-growing companies in the world, and we're building the brand and creative studio to match. We make global campaigns, partnerships, film, design, and social at real scale, for businesses and for workers in almost every country there is.

We're looking for someone exceptional to raise the bar on what we make. This is a hands-on role. You'd set the standard by making the work.

The role

Deel is a truly global, people-first brand, and it's taking off. We're looking for a creative director who works at the front edge of AI-native production across video and design. Most AI creative work is technically impressive and creatively empty. Some of it is good work that used AI somewhere in the pipeline. We think there's a real discipline in between, and we want you to build it here. You'd define how we make this work, and you'd prove it by making it. This is a hands-on role.

What You'll Make

AI-native creative. Work where generative tools are central to how it's made, at a standard the category hasn't reached.
The stack. Our AI creative tooling and the workflows around it, including the principles for where we don't use it.
Video and motion. Brand films, campaign work, and product storytelling that blend traditional and AI-led production.
A repeatable method. Something the rest of the team can use, so the capability outlives any one project.

What You Bring

At least ten years across video, motion, or design, with direction as well as production.
Recent work made or directed with generative AI that stands up as creative work first.
Deep knowledge of the current tooling, and clear judgment about where it breaks.
Proven ability to build a workflow other people can actually use.
A point of view on likeness, disclosure, and provenance. We take these seriously.

What Would Set You Apart

A reel with range across live-action, motion, and generative work.
Experience establishing an AI practice inside a creative team.
A public point of view on AI in creative work.

Who You'll Work With

You'll sit inside the creative studio and work alongside our Creative Director, the video and motion teams, and the brand designers who'll build on what you establish.

How We Work

We're a studio, not a request queue. People here make things rather than manage from a distance. We use AI seriously, and we're deliberate about where we don't.

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview

The Associate Director plays a critical role in supporting the growth and risk‑management objectives of the portfolio. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.
Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies

Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.

new_jobs.title: Director of Financial Reporting
new_jobs.description:
SETUP
: Mostly remote, only required 1-2 times/month in office. Located in North York, ON

CONTRACT
: 18 months

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.

new_jobs.title: Director, Private Capital, Financial Services
new_jobs.description:
The opportunity

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board (Ontario Teachers') is a global investor with net assets of ~$279 billion as of December 31, 2025. Ontario Teachers’ is a fully funded defined benefit pension plan, and it invests in a broad array of asset classes to deliver retirement security for 346,000 working members and pensioners. Our Private Capital group deploys ~$60 billion across direct private equity investments and private equity funds globally.

The Director will be a senior member of our Financial Services investment team — partnering with our Senior Managing Directors and Managing Directors to source, diligence, execute, and direct private equity investments in the Financial Services sector. This is a development seat with a clear path toward independent deal leadership for a candidate who has already built a strong foundation in private equity investing.

Who You'll Work With

Reporting to the Managing Director, the role will be part of a deal team comprising analysts, associates, principals, directors, and managing directors, supported by third-party consultants, operating executives, and legal and accounting advisors dedicated to each transaction.

The Financial Services team invests across sub-sectors including Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments, with particular need to understand the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping the sector. The role will also potentially partner with colleagues in OTPP's global offices on international investment and / or cross asset class opportunities in Financial Services.

What You'll Do

Serve as a key member of deal teams — conducting industry and company due diligence, building financial models, arranging debt financing, negotiating legal documents, and preparing written recommendations for the Underwriting Committee.
Lead or co-lead individual deals and workstreams with oversight from the SMD or MD; own specific diligence streams (financial, operational, commercial, legal, tax, insurance) end-to-end.
Post-close, remain actively involved with portfolio companies — often as board observer or board member — working with management on strategy, value creation, M&A, and refinancing.
Contribute to deal flow generation through desk research, consultant relationships, operating executive networks, conferences, and relationships with management teams.
Lead sub-sector deep dives and thematic research as the team evolves its coverage strategy, including emerging AI, regulatory, and digitization themes.
Manage and develop analysts, associates, and principals on deal teams; provide direct mentorship on diligence, modeling, judgment, and communication.
Work in a highly collaborative manner, bringing a complex network of stakeholders along (Global and Sector SMDs, MDs, deal teams, Portfolio Solutions team, international office leaders, portfolio companies, etc.). Strike the appropriate balance of being a confident decision-maker and an inclusive leader.
Build a network of operating executives, CEOs, consultants, bankers, and peer sponsors; progress toward independent deal sourcing by the end of Director tenure.
Develop value creation expertise in close partnership with the SMD and MDs; contribute to portfolio company initiatives as assigned.
Exercise judgment within deal teams and surface recommendations to the MD or SMD; lead individual workstreams and, over time, full deals with oversight.
Provide disciplined thinking, sound judgment, and courage of conviction, with a willingness to take balanced, thesis-driven risk. Intervene directly and effectively when required and escalate issues early.
Work cross-functionally and collaboratively with other teams to ensure continued alignment with OTPP's mission, vision, and values — including supporting and sharing knowledge with other areas of Investments and responding to ad hoc requests.

What You'll Need

~10+ years of meaningful work experience, including several years of recent private equity investing. Active M&A in a senior role in corporate development would also be considered. Supplemented by previous experience in management consulting, investment banking, and/or corporations (preferably corporate development or similar roles).
Experience playing a lead role on deal workstreams, including conducting due diligence, leading multiple diligence streams (financial, operational, legal, tax, insurance), arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Direct investment exposure to Financial Services preferred.
Familiarity with Financial Services sector dynamics — particularly Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments — and the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping them
Some experience serving on “for profit” Boards of Directors or board committees a plus.
Strong academic background, with a financial designation (MBA, CFA, CBV, or CA strongly preferred).
Experience playing a leading role in the investment process, including conducting due diligence, arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Strong negotiating skills.
Ability to balance priorities, work independently, lead projects, and thrive in a high-performance team environment.
Very strong analytical and quantitative skills to perform and guide in-depth, innovative, critical analysis.
Deep understanding of fundamental investment analysis and private equity value creation.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build constructive relationships with internal and external parties, particularly management teams, boards, and senior advisors.
Strong communication skills, both oral and written, including IC paper authorship and presentation.
Willingness and ability to travel across North America and globally.

What We’re Offering

Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development
Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage
Retirement income through a defined benefit pension plan
The opportunity to invest back into the fund through our Deferred Incentive Program
A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working
Competitive time off
Our Flexible Travel Program gives you the option to work abroad in another region/country for up to a month each year
Employee discount programs including Edvantage and Perkopolis

At Ontario Teachers', diversity is one of our core strengths. We take pride in ensuring that the people we hire and the culture we create, reflect and embrace diversity of thought, background and experience. Through our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion strategy and our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), we celebrate diversity and foster inclusion through events for colleagues to connect for professional development, networking & mentoring. We are building an inclusive and equitable workplace where our talent is respected, accepted and empowered to be themselves.
